model.name: AI Agent
model.purpose: Describe an AI agent as a governed, identifiable non-human actor that holds delegated authority, is bound to tools and memory, operates under policy and oversight, and can be inspected, released, constrained and retired by an accountable party.
model.scope_statement: The subject is the durable, versioned agent definition plus the deployment context that makes it operable: identity and classification, capability and protocol surface, delegated authority and credentials, memory and data handling, lifecycle and runtime limits, oversight, and assurance evidence. The model is projection-neutral: JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MCP endpoints, graph stores and MongoDB collections are storage or interface projections of the same semantics. External standards are recorded as alignments only; no conformance is asserted without cited evidence.
in_scope: Agent identity, designation, aliases and version identity of a released agent definition
Architectural archetype, autonomy level, regulatory role and risk classification
Constituent bindings: invoked models, referenced configuration artefacts, callable sub-agents
Declared capability surface: bound tools, accessible resources, declared skills, refusal scope
Protocol bindings, capability advertisement, revision negotiation, descriptor authenticity
Delegated authority: acting principal, delegation chain, credential scope, token audience binding
Action authorisation policy, deny boundaries, consent and human-approval gates
Memory store inventory, write authority, memory provenance and integrity controls
Data categories, purpose limitation, residency constraints, retention and deletion duties
Lifecycle states, release approval, rollback, suspension and decommission obligations
Runtime operating envelope: step, time, concurrency and cost limits and breach behaviour
Human oversight affordances, intervention records, incident handling
Pre-deployment evaluation, in-service monitoring, telemetry conformance, conformity evidence
out_of_scope: Model training, weights, fine-tuning data and model cards, which belong to the AI system or model sibling
Individual execution traces, spans, token counts and per-run outcomes, which belong to the agent run model
Instruction text, templating and variable schemas of prompts or agent configuration files
Natural-person records, employment and human competence records
Internal implementation of the tools, APIs and services an agent calls
Hosting, network and compute infrastructure topology
Embodied actuation, motion planning and physical safety of robots
Commercial contracting, billing and agent-to-agent payment settlement
Any claim of certification or regulatory compliance not backed by cited evidence

boundary_notes.distinction: The AI system is the product placed on the market and carries system-level obligations; the agent is one actor it exposes. Model inventory, system risk management and market placement stay in WM-AI-001; actor-level authority, tool bindings, memory and oversight stay here.

A run is a bounded execution event with traces and outcomes; the agent is the durable actor that runs reference. Correlation identifiers and version references live here; spans, messages and token usage live in WM-AI-004.
The configuration artefact carries instruction content and parameters; this model carries only the reference, the pinning mode and the approval status of that binding.
Human principals, approvers and overseers are references to the person or party model. This model records the delegation relation and accountable role, not the human's own attributes.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Tool, server or external service model
boundary_notes.distinction: A tool's own schema, endpoint contract and operator are a separate subject. This model records the binding, its effect class, trust status and approval, not the tool's internal definition.
Issuance mechanics, key material and authorisation-server internals stay in the identity domain; this model records which scopes and audiences an agent may hold and under whose delegation.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol Specification
sources.version_or_date: Revision 2026-07-28 (current revision at time of access)
sources.relevance: Normative source for tool, resource and prompt primitives, per-request capability negotiation, extensions such as Tasks and Skills, and the user-consent and tool-safety principles including treating tool descriptions as untrusted.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol - Authorization
sources.relevance: Normative requirements for OAuth 2.1 flows, protected resource metadata discovery, resource indicators, token audience validation, prohibition of token pass-through and confused-deputy mitigation.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Defines Agent as a responsibility-bearing thing distinct from Activity and Entity, and supplies wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf, used, wasDerivedFrom, qualified associations and Plan for delegation and provenance modelling.

sources.title: RFC 3339 - Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp grammar requiring full date, seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; basis for the model's time rules and the separation of event time from ingestion time.

sources.title: RFC 9728 - OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata
sources.relevance: Defines resource identifier, authorization_servers, scopes_supported and WWW-Authenticate based discovery; supports capability advertisement, scope declaration and audience-bound access for agent-reachable resources.

sources.title: AI Risk Management Framework (NIST AI 100-1)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Voluntary framework organised around Govern, Map, Measure and Manage; grounds the governance, classification, measurement, monitoring and lifecycle-management structure of this model.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Companion profile naming generative-AI risk categories including data privacy, information integrity, information security and human-AI configuration; used for data handling, evaluation and risk findings, with its non-agentic scope recorded as a conflict.

sources.title: AI Act - Regulatory framework for artificial intelligence
sources.organization: European Commission, Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology
sources.version_or_date: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; in force 1 August 2024; general application 2 August 2026
sources.relevance: Official summary of risk tiers, provider and deployer roles and high-risk obligations including activity logging for traceability, technical documentation, human oversight, robustness and transparency duties.

sources.title: Article 14: Human Oversight - EU Artificial Intelligence Act
sources.organization: EU Artificial Intelligence Act information portal (Future of Life Institute)
sources.relevance: Reproduces Article 14 text used for the oversight findings: measures proportionate to risk and autonomy level, comprehension of capabilities and limitations, automation-bias awareness and a stop mechanism. Must be re-verified against the Official Journal text.

sources.title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification
sources.version_or_date: Version 1.0.0 (latest released at time of access)
sources.relevance: Defines the Agent Card (name, description, url, provider, version, protocolVersion, capabilities, skills, securitySchemes, signatures), task lifecycle states and message, part and artifact structures used for capability advertisement and discovery.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions for Generative AI - Agent spans
sources.version_or_date: main branch as accessed; attributes at Development stability
sources.relevance: Defines gen_ai.operation.name values including create_agent, invoke_agent, plan and execute_tool, plus gen_ai.agent.id, gen_ai.agent.name, gen_ai.agent.description and gen_ai.conversation.id, and warns against recording transient in-memory agent instance identifiers.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-207: Zero Trust Architecture
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Establishes per-session authentication and authorisation as discrete functions, resource-centric protection and the absence of implicit trust from location or ownership; grounds the authorisation, delegation and monitoring findings.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
sources.version_or_date: Page states a 2026 edition dated 4 August 2026 while listing earlier-edition entry titles
sources.relevance: Community risk taxonomy naming excessive agency, prompt injection, supply-chain and sensitive-information-disclosure risks; used to shape threat and limit findings, with its internal version inconsistency recorded as a conflict.

bundles.name: Agent identity and constitution
bundles.description: What the agent is as a governed entity: authoritative identifier, designation, version identity, archetype and autonomy class, regulatory role, constituent bindings and definition provenance.
bundles.rationale: Provenance modelling treats an agent as a responsibility-bearing thing separate from the activities it performs; telemetry conventions require a stable non-transient agent identifier; agent-card publication requires a versioned public designation; and regulation attaches obligations to a classified system and to named provider and deployer roles.

layers.name: Identity and designation
layers.description: How the agent is uniquely designated, how public and protocol-scoped names relate to the primary key, and how a released version is identified over time.

findings.name: Agent identifier and designation
findings.description: The primary identifier designating this agent, the published human-readable designation, and the alias set that resolves to the same agent across protocols and registries.

questions.text: Which authoritative master-system identifier designates this agent, and which system issues it?
What human-readable name, description and purpose statement are published for the agent?
Which alternate or protocol-scoped identifiers resolve to this same agent?
How is a durable agent definition distinguished from a transient in-memory agent instance?
answer_data: Reason a transient identifier is or is not recorded

data_elements.name: Agent identifier
data_elements.description: Primary key for the agent, assigned per the identity priority of the adopting Dimension.

data_elements.name: Agent designation
data_elements.description: Human-readable name published for humans and capability descriptors.

data_elements.name: Agent description
data_elements.description: Free-form statement of what the agent is for.

data_elements.name: Alias identifier
data_elements.description: Protocol-scoped or legacy identifier resolving to this agent; never a primary key.

data_elements.name: Governed namespace IRI
data_elements.description: Resolvable HTTPS namespace under which the agent identifier is minted.

artifacts.name: Agent identity record
artifacts.description: Authoritative record binding primary identifier, designation, namespace and alias set, with the issuing system named.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the authoritative master-system identifier; aliases are attributes, never keys.

findings.name: Agent version and change identity
findings.description: How a released agent definition is versioned, which fields are frozen so a version denotes one behaviour contract, when each version is effective and superseded, and its derivation lineage.

questions.text: What versioning scheme identifies a released agent definition, and which changes force a new version?
From which instant is each agent version effective, and when was it superseded?
Which fields are frozen at release so that a version identifier always denotes the same behaviour contract?
Which prior agent version was this version derived from?

data_elements.name: Agent version identifier
data_elements.description: Released version label of the agent definition.

data_elements.name: Version effective from
data_elements.description: Instant at which the version became the governing definition.

data_elements.name: Version superseded at
data_elements.description: Instant at which a later version replaced this one.

data_elements.name: Derived-from version
data_elements.description: Reference to the predecessor version this definition was derived from.

data_elements.name: Frozen field set
data_elements.description: Fields immutable for the life of the version.

artifacts.name: Agent version manifest
artifacts.description: Immutable manifest of one released version listing frozen fields, effective interval, predecessor and canonical digest.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Composite of agent identifier plus version identifier; never keyed by release date.

layers.name: Classification and autonomy
layers.description: How the agent is typed by architecture and by the autonomy it may exercise, and how it is classified under applicable regulatory and risk frameworks.

findings.name: Agent typology and autonomy level
findings.description: The architectural archetype implemented and the autonomy the agent may exercise without a human decision point, including whether it may act on its own initiative.

questions.text: What level of autonomy is the agent authorised to exercise without a human decision point?
Which architectural archetype does the agent implement: single actor, orchestrator, sub-agent or scripted workflow?
Can the agent initiate activity without a human or upstream request, and under which trigger conditions?
How often is the assigned autonomy level re-justified against observed behaviour?

data_elements.name: Autonomy level code
data_elements.description: Coded degree of independent action permitted to the agent.

data_elements.name: Architectural archetype code
data_elements.description: Coded structural role of the agent in its deployment.

data_elements.name: Initiative mode
data_elements.description: Whether the agent is reactive, scheduled or self-initiating.

data_elements.name: Autonomy review interval
data_elements.description: Maximum period between re-justifications of the autonomy level.

artifacts.name: Autonomy classification statement
artifacts.description: Signed statement recording assigned autonomy level and archetype, the scale used, justification and review schedule.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier plus version identifier; superseded rather than overwritten.

findings.name: Regulatory role and risk classification
findings.description: Which regulatory role the operator holds per jurisdiction, the risk tier and use-case category, the disclosure duties that follow, and the evidence supporting the classification.

questions.text: Is the operator of this agent a provider or a deployer in each jurisdiction where it operates?
Which regulatory risk tier and use-case category does the agent fall into?
Which disclosure duties apply when the agent interacts with natural persons or emits synthetic content?
What evidence supports the assigned risk classification, and who signed it off?

data_elements.name: Regulatory role code
data_elements.description: Provider, deployer or other role held per jurisdiction.

data_elements.name: Risk tier code
data_elements.description: Assigned risk tier under the applicable framework.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction scope
data_elements.description: Jurisdictions in which the agent is placed, used, or whose output is used.

data_elements.name: Disclosure obligation
data_elements.description: Transparency duty triggered by interaction or output type.

data_elements.name: Classification decision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the signed classification decision.

artifacts.name: Regulatory classification dossier
artifacts.description: Dossier recording role determination, risk tier, jurisdictional scope, disclosure duties and approving authority.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier plus jurisdiction; versioned on any re-classification.

layers.name: Constitution and provenance
layers.description: Which components the agent is assembled from, and who authored, derived and approved the definition.

findings.name: Agent constituent bindings
findings.description: The models invoked, the configuration artefacts governing instructions, the callable sub-agents, and whether each binding is pinned or floating.

questions.text: Which model or models does the agent invoke, and are those bindings pinned or floating?
Which configuration artefact governs the agent's instructions, and at which version?
Which sub-agents or delegate agents may this agent instantiate or call?
What happens to the agent's identity and approvals when a bound component is substituted?

data_elements.name: Model binding
data_elements.description: Reference to an invoked model with its pinning mode.

data_elements.name: Configuration reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the governing prompt or agent-configuration artefact and version.

data_elements.name: Sub-agent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an agent this agent may call or instantiate.

data_elements.name: Binding pin mode
data_elements.description: Whether bindings are pinned to an exact version or allowed to float.

artifacts.name: Agent composition manifest
artifacts.description: Manifest enumerating model, configuration and sub-agent bindings with pin modes and re-approval rules.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier plus version identifier; immutable once its version is released.

findings.name: Definition provenance and attribution
findings.description: Who authored, derived and approved the definition, how responsibility for outputs is attributed, and how the provenance record itself is protected.

questions.text: Which party authored and which party approved this agent definition?
From which template, framework or upstream agent definition was this definition derived?
How is responsibility for the agent's outputs attributed back to a responsible party?
How is the provenance record protected against later undetected modification?

data_elements.name: Authored by
data_elements.description: Party or agent that authored the definition.

data_elements.name: Approved by
data_elements.description: Party that approved the definition for use.

data_elements.name: Derived from
data_elements.description: Upstream definition, template or framework the definition derives from.

data_elements.name: Provenance statement
data_elements.description: Qualified association linking activity, agent and plan for the definition's creation.

data_elements.name: Definition digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical form of the definition.

artifacts.name: Agent provenance graph
artifacts.description: Provenance record expressing authorship, approval, derivation and attribution as qualified relations between entities, activities and agents.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent version identifier; each assertion carries its own asserting party and time.

bundles.name: Capability and interoperability
bundles.description: What the agent can do and how that surface is declared, discovered, negotiated and trusted by other parties.
bundles.rationale: Tool and resource primitives, skill declarations and capability descriptors are the contract other systems rely on; the same sources that define them also warn that descriptor content is untrusted and that protocol revisions change the available primitives.

layers.name: Capability surface
layers.description: The concrete tool and resource bindings the agent holds and the skills it declares to callers.

findings.name: Tool and resource bindings
findings.description: Which tools and data resources the agent is bound to, which cause irreversible effects, how each provider is vetted, and how a binding change is detected and re-approved.

questions.text: Which tools, functions and data resources is the agent bound to, and from which servers or providers?
Which bound tools are read-only and which cause irreversible or externally visible effects?
How is each tool provider vetted, and are tool descriptions treated as untrusted content?
How is a change to a bound tool's schema, description or endpoint detected and re-approved?

data_elements.name: Tool binding
data_elements.description: One bound tool or function with identifier, provider and approval status.

data_elements.name: Tool server reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the server or provider exposing the tool.

data_elements.name: Effect class
data_elements.description: Coded reversibility and external-visibility class of a bound tool.

data_elements.name: Tool descriptor digest
data_elements.description: Digest of the approved tool descriptor used to detect drift.

data_elements.name: Resource scope
data_elements.description: Data resources and URI boundaries the agent may read.

artifacts.name: Tool binding registry entry
artifacts.description: Per-binding record holding provider, effect class, vetting decision, approved descriptor digest and re-approval state.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Composite of agent identifier, tool identifier and provider identifier; descriptor digest carried as an attribute.

findings.name: Skill and task declaration
findings.description: The task types the agent declares, the input and output modalities per skill, the requests it must refuse or route away, and the evidence each declared skill is met.

questions.text: Which skills or task types does the agent declare that it can perform?
Which input and output content types does the agent accept and produce per skill?
Which requests must the agent refuse or route elsewhere?
What evidence shows the agent performs each declared skill at the stated quality?

data_elements.name: Skill declaration
data_elements.description: One declared skill with identifier, description and scope.

data_elements.name: Input modes
data_elements.description: Accepted input content types for the agent or a skill.

data_elements.name: Output modes
data_elements.description: Produced output content types for the agent or a skill.

data_elements.name: Refusal scope
data_elements.description: Request classes the agent must refuse or route away.

artifacts.name: Agent capability card
artifacts.description: Published descriptor listing declared skills, modalities, refusal scope and supporting evidence references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier plus version identifier; the descriptor name field is a display alias, not a key.

layers.name: Protocol conformance and discovery
layers.description: Which protocols and revisions the agent speaks, how it advertises and negotiates them, and how consumers verify a descriptor is authentic.

findings.name: Protocol conformance and advertisement
findings.description: Protocol bindings and revisions per endpoint, negotiation and failure behaviour, descriptor authenticity, and the evidence behind any conformance claim.

questions.text: Which agent and tool protocols, at which revisions, does the agent speak on each endpoint?
How does the agent negotiate protocol revisions and behave when no mutually supported revision exists?
How can a consumer verify that a published capability descriptor genuinely belongs to this agent?
Which conformance claims are asserted, and what test evidence supports them?

data_elements.name: Protocol binding
data_elements.description: A protocol offered by the agent with its transport and role.

data_elements.name: Endpoint URI
data_elements.description: Canonical resource URI on which the protocol is offered.

data_elements.name: Supported revisions
data_elements.description: Protocol revisions the agent accepts.

data_elements.name: Descriptor signature
data_elements.description: Signature over the published capability descriptor.

data_elements.name: Conformance evidence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to test evidence supporting a conformance claim.

artifacts.name: Published agent descriptor
artifacts.description: Externally retrievable, signed descriptor combining identity, skills, protocol revisions, endpoints and security schemes for discovery.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Addressed by canonical resource URI; bound to the agent identifier inside the payload and verified by signature.

bundles.name: Authority, delegation and access control
bundles.description: On whose behalf the agent acts, what it may do, which credentials carry that permission, and where a human decision is required before it acts.
bundles.rationale: Provenance modelling makes delegation explicit through acting-on-behalf-of relations; authorization specifications require audience-bound tokens and forbid pass-through; zero-trust guidance requires per-session authorisation with no implicit trust; and protocol trust principles require explicit user consent before tool invocation.

layers.name: Delegation and credentials
layers.description: The chain from an originating human principal to the agent and its sub-agents, and the credentials carrying the granted authority.

findings.name: Principal and delegation chain
findings.description: The principal on whose behalf the agent acts, the full chain to sub-agents, the non-delegable authorities, and each delegation's validity window.

questions.text: On whose behalf is the agent acting for a given activity, and how is that principal identified?
What is the full delegation chain from the originating human principal to this agent and its sub-agents?
Which authorities may never be sub-delegated onward to another agent?
For how long and under which conditions does a delegation remain valid?

data_elements.name: Acting principal reference
data_elements.description: Party on whose behalf the agent acts.

data_elements.name: Delegation chain
data_elements.description: Ordered sequence of delegating parties from originating principal to acting agent.

data_elements.name: Non-delegable authority
data_elements.description: Authority that must not be passed onward to a sub-agent.

data_elements.name: Delegation valid until
data_elements.description: Instant after which the delegation no longer holds.

artifacts.name: Delegation grant record
artifacts.description: Record of one delegation: granting principal, receiving agent, scope, non-delegable exclusions and validity window.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by grant identifier issued by the granting authority; parties referenced by their own authoritative identifiers.

findings.name: Credential scope and token binding
findings.description: The credentials the agent may present, their binding to an intended resource audience, the minimum scope per skill, and rotation and revocation.

questions.text: Which credentials, tokens or keys can the agent present, and who issued each?
How is each token bound to its intended resource audience, and is pass-through forbidden?
What is the minimum scope set required for each declared skill?
How are agent credentials rotated, revoked and re-issued?

data_elements.name: Credential reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to a credential the agent may present; key material is never stored in the model.

data_elements.name: Granted scopes
data_elements.description: Authorisation scopes attached to a credential.

data_elements.name: Token audience
data_elements.description: Canonical resource identifier a token is valid for.

data_elements.name: Rotation interval
data_elements.description: Maximum period before a credential must be rotated.

data_elements.name: Revocation state
data_elements.description: Current revocation status of a credential.

artifacts.name: Agent credential scope map
artifacts.description: Map from declared skills to minimum credentials, scopes and resource audiences, with rotation and revocation state.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier plus version identifier; credentials referenced by issuer-assigned identifiers, never by value.

layers.name: Permission boundaries and consent
layers.description: The policy authorising each action, the categorical prohibitions, the bounded blast radius, and the points where a human must consent.

findings.name: Action authorisation policy
findings.description: Which policy decision point authorises each action, which actions are categorically forbidden, how far a single action can reach, and how an emergency deviation is approved.

questions.text: Which policy decision point authorises each agent action, and is the decision made per request?
Which actions, targets or environments are categorically forbidden to the agent?
What is the maximum blast radius of a single authorised action, and how is it bounded?
How is an emergency deviation from policy requested, approved and recorded?

data_elements.name: Authorisation policy reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the governing authorisation policy and its version.

data_elements.name: Deny rule
data_elements.description: Categorical prohibition on an action, target or environment.

data_elements.name: Environment scope
data_elements.description: Environments in which the agent may act, such as sandbox, staging or production.

data_elements.name: Maximum impact bound
data_elements.description: Quantitative ceiling on the effect of a single authorised action.

data_elements.name: Policy override record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an approved emergency deviation.

artifacts.name: Agent authorisation policy
artifacts.description: Versioned policy defining decision points, allow and deny rules, environment scope, impact bounds and override procedure.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by policy identifier and version; bound to agent versions by explicit reference rather than name matching.

findings.name: Human approval and consent gates
findings.description: Which operations require explicit human consent, what evidences that consent, whether approval is per action, per session or standing, and how rubber-stamping is resisted.

questions.text: Which operations require explicit user consent before the agent may proceed?
What is recorded to evidence that consent or approval was given, by whom and when?
Does a granted approval cover a single action, a session or a standing authorisation?
How is the oversight interface protected against approval fatigue and rubber-stamping?

data_elements.name: Consent gate
data_elements.description: An operation class requiring explicit human approval.

data_elements.name: Approval record
data_elements.description: Structured evidence of a granted or refused approval.

data_elements.name: Approval granularity
data_elements.description: Whether an approval is per action, per session or standing.

data_elements.name: Approver reference
data_elements.description: Party that granted or refused the approval.

artifacts.name: Consent and approval log
artifacts.description: Append-only log of consent prompts, decisions, approvers, presented content and validity windows.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Sequential entry identifier per agent; each entry carries event time and ingestion time separately.

layers.name: Accountable roles
layers.description: Which named parties are accountable for the agent, how duties are separated, and how accountability survives organisational change.

findings.name: Ownership and accountability assignment
findings.description: The organisation and roles accountable in production, separation of build, approval and operation duties, escalation contacts and response targets, and accountability transfer.

questions.text: Which named organisation and role is accountable for this agent in production?
How are build, approval and operation duties separated across roles?
Who is contactable, and within what response time, when the agent misbehaves?
What happens to accountability when the owning team, vendor or contract changes?

data_elements.name: Accountable organisation
data_elements.description: Organisation answerable for the agent's operation.

data_elements.name: Accountable role
data_elements.description: Named roles holding defined duties for the agent.

data_elements.name: Escalation contact
data_elements.description: Contact route for misbehaviour or incident escalation.

data_elements.name: Response time target
data_elements.description: Committed maximum time to first human response.

data_elements.name: Handover record
data_elements.description: Reference to a recorded transfer of accountability.

artifacts.name: Agent accountability register entry
artifacts.description: Register entry naming the accountable organisation, roles, duty separation, escalation routes and handover history.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier; historical assignments retained as time-bounded rows rather than overwritten.

bundles.name: Memory, state and data governance
bundles.description: What the agent remembers, what may write into that memory, which data it may process for which purpose, and how long anything is kept.
bundles.rationale: Durable agent memory is a governed data store with its own privacy, integrity and retention duties; risk taxonomies name data privacy, information integrity and poisoning as first-order concerns, and protocol trust principles forbid transmitting user data without consent.

layers.name: Memory architecture
layers.description: Which stores hold agent state, how they are scoped and isolated, and how their contents are kept trustworthy.

findings.name: Memory store inventory
findings.description: The stores read and written, which persist beyond a session and where, how memory is isolated between tenants and sessions, and which source wins on conflict.

questions.text: Which memory stores does the agent read from and write to, and what is each store's scope?
Which memory persists beyond a session, and in which storage locality is it held?
How is memory isolated between tenants, users and sessions?
When stored memory conflicts with current instructions or retrieved context, which source prevails?

data_elements.name: Memory store
data_elements.description: One store the agent reads or writes, with kind and scope.

data_elements.name: Persistence scope
data_elements.description: Whether memory is per turn, per session or durable.

data_elements.name: Storage locality
data_elements.description: Physical or logical region where durable memory resides.

data_elements.name: Isolation boundary
data_elements.description: Boundary enforced between tenants, users or sessions.

data_elements.name: Precedence rule
data_elements.description: Rule resolving conflicts between memory, instructions and retrieved context.

artifacts.name: Memory store inventory record
artifacts.description: Inventory of agent memory stores with kind, scope, locality, isolation boundary and precedence rules.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier plus store identifier; store identifiers assigned by the owning data platform.

findings.name: Memory write integrity
findings.description: What may write into durable memory and under whose authority, the provenance each item carries, controls against poisoning, and correction or quarantine of bad items.

questions.text: What is permitted to write into durable agent memory, and under whose authority?
For each memory item, what records its origin, observation time and confidence?
Which controls detect and contain poisoned or adversarially injected memory?
How is an incorrect memory item corrected, quarantined or rolled back?

data_elements.name: Write permission rule
data_elements.description: Rule stating which sources may write to which memory store.

data_elements.name: Memory item provenance
data_elements.description: Origin, deriving activity and asserting party for a memory item.

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the remembered fact was observed, distinct from write time.

data_elements.name: Integrity check
data_elements.description: Digest or validation applied to a stored memory item.

data_elements.name: Quarantine state
data_elements.description: Whether an item is active, quarantined or withdrawn.

artifacts.name: Memory item provenance record
artifacts.description: Per-item record of origin, observation time, writing authority, integrity check and quarantine state.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item identifier assigned by the memory store, referenced with the store identifier to stay unique across stores.

layers.name: Data protection and retention
layers.description: Which data categories the agent may process for which purposes, and how long each record class is kept before deletion.

findings.name: Data category and purpose limits
findings.description: Categories of personal, confidential or regulated data permitted, declared purposes for each, cross-boundary transfer conditions, and verification of minimisation.

questions.text: Which categories of personal, confidential or regulated data may the agent process?
For which declared purposes may each data category be used, and what use is forbidden?
Under which conditions may data leave a jurisdiction, tenant or trust boundary?
How is it verified that the agent requests only the data it needs?

data_elements.name: Data category
data_elements.description: Class of data the agent is permitted to process.

data_elements.name: Permitted purpose
data_elements.description: Declared purpose for which a data category may be used.

data_elements.name: Transfer condition
data_elements.description: Condition permitting movement across a boundary.

data_elements.name: Residency constraint
data_elements.description: Jurisdictional constraint on where data may be stored or processed.

artifacts.name: Agent data handling statement
artifacts.description: Statement of data categories, permitted purposes, prohibited uses, transfer conditions and residency constraints.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier plus version identifier; re-issued whenever categories or purposes change.

findings.name: Retention and deletion rules
findings.description: How long each class of record, log and memory is retained and on what clock, deletion triggers and verification, legal holds, and resolution of conflicting duties.

questions.text: How long is each class of agent record, log and memory retained, and from which clock does the period run?
Which events trigger deletion, and how is deletion verified across replicas and backups?
How does a legal hold or open investigation suspend normal deletion?
How are conflicting duties resolved between audit retention and erasure rights?

data_elements.name: Retention class
data_elements.description: Class assigned to a record type for retention purposes.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Duration for which a retention class is kept.

data_elements.name: Deletion verification
data_elements.description: Method and result proving deletion across all copies.

data_elements.name: Legal hold flag
data_elements.description: Whether deletion is currently suspended by a hold.

data_elements.name: Retention conflict rule
data_elements.description: Rule resolving competing retention and erasure duties.

artifacts.name: Retention schedule entry
artifacts.description: Entry binding a record class to its retention period, clock start, deletion trigger, hold handling and verification method.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by retention class identifier issued by the owning data governance function, scoped to the agent identifier.

bundles.name: Lifecycle and runtime operation
bundles.description: How an agent moves through its governed states, how releases are approved and rolled back, and how it is bounded and overseen while running.
bundles.rationale: Risk-management guidance organises AI work as a governed lifecycle with explicit management actions; regulation requires high-risk systems to be effectively overseen by natural persons while in use, including intervention and stop; and excessive agency is a named risk that must be bounded by explicit operating limits.

layers.name: Lifecycle and change control
layers.description: The legal states of an agent, transitions between them, and the approval and rollback controls governing releases.

findings.name: Agent lifecycle state model
findings.description: States an agent may occupy, legal transitions, preconditions for production, conditions forcing suspension, and decommission obligations.

questions.text: Which lifecycle states may an agent occupy, and which transitions between them are legal?
What must be true before an agent may move into an active production state?
Which conditions force immediate suspension or withdrawal of the agent?
What must be preserved, migrated or destroyed when the agent is retired?

data_elements.name: Lifecycle state
data_elements.description: Current governed state of the agent.

data_elements.name: State entered at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the current state was entered.

data_elements.name: Allowed transition
data_elements.description: Legal transition from one state to another with its guard condition.

data_elements.name: Suspension reason
data_elements.description: Coded reason for suspension or withdrawal.

data_elements.name: Decommission plan reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the plan governing retirement obligations.

artifacts.name: Agent lifecycle state record
artifacts.description: Append-only history of lifecycle states with entry instants, actors, reasons and guard evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Sequential transition identifier per agent; current state derived from the latest entry, never a lone mutable field.

findings.name: Release approval and rollback
findings.description: Approval gates before production, which changes are material and force re-approval, rollback speed and target, and the record proving who approved on what evidence.

questions.text: Which approval gates must be passed before an agent version reaches production?
Which changes count as material and therefore require re-approval?
How quickly can a released agent version be rolled back, and to which known-good state?
What record proves who approved a release, on what evidence and at what time?

data_elements.name: Release gate
data_elements.description: A required approval gate with owner and outcome.

data_elements.name: Change materiality
data_elements.description: Coded materiality of a change to the agent definition.

data_elements.name: Rollback target version
data_elements.description: Known-good version to which the agent can be reverted.

data_elements.name: Rollback time objective
data_elements.description: Committed maximum time to complete a rollback.

data_elements.name: Approval timestamp
data_elements.description: Instant at which a gate decision was recorded.

artifacts.name: Release approval record
artifacts.description: Record of gate outcomes, approvers, supporting evidence, materiality assessment and rollback plan for one agent version.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent version identifier plus sequential release attempt number.

layers.name: Runtime control and execution linkage
layers.description: How humans supervise and stop the agent, how its consumption is bounded, and how running activity ties back to the exact agent version.

findings.name: Human oversight and intervention
findings.description: Affordances letting a competent person understand, monitor and interrupt the agent in use, the stop mechanism and residual state, counter-measures to automation bias, and intervention records.

questions.text: Which interface affordances let a competent person understand, monitor and interrupt the agent while it is in use?
How is the agent stopped mid-task, and what state does a stop leave behind?
How does the oversight design counter automation bias and over-reliance on agent output?
What is recorded when a human overrides, corrects or halts the agent?

data_elements.name: Oversight affordance
data_elements.description: Interface capability supporting understanding, monitoring or interruption.

data_elements.name: Stop mechanism
data_elements.description: Means by which operation is interrupted or halted.

data_elements.name: Overseer competence requirement
data_elements.description: Competence, training or authority required of the assigned overseer.

data_elements.name: Intervention event
data_elements.description: Recorded human override, correction or halt.

artifacts.name: Oversight intervention log
artifacts.description: Append-only log of human interventions with type, actor, target activity, event time and ingestion time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Sequential entry identifier per agent; each entry references the run or activity identifier issued by the execution system.

findings.name: Operating limits and budgets
findings.description: Caps on steps, tool calls, recursion depth and wall-clock time per task, token, compute and monetary budgets, the concurrency ceiling, and defined breach behaviour.

questions.text: What limits cap the agent's steps, tool calls, recursion depth and wall-clock time per task?
Which token, compute and monetary budgets apply, and what happens when they are exhausted?
How many concurrent tasks and sessions may the agent hold, and how is contention resolved?
What is the defined behaviour on limit breach: halt, degrade or escalate?

data_elements.name: Maximum steps
data_elements.description: Cap on reasoning or action steps within one task.

data_elements.name: Maximum tool calls
data_elements.description: Cap on tool invocations within one task.

data_elements.name: Task time limit
data_elements.description: Wall-clock ceiling for one task.

data_elements.name: Cost budget
data_elements.description: Token, compute or monetary budget with unit and window.

data_elements.name: Concurrency limit
data_elements.description: Maximum simultaneous tasks or sessions.

data_elements.name: Breach action
data_elements.description: Defined behaviour when a limit is exceeded.

artifacts.name: Operating envelope specification
artifacts.description: Specification of step, time, concurrency and cost limits with breach behaviour and notification targets.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier plus version identifier; enforced values referenced by the runtime rather than duplicated.

findings.name: Run and session linkage
findings.description: How an execution record references the exact agent version, which correlation identifiers tie activity into one task, how event time is separated from observation time, and what must be captured for reconstruction.

questions.text: How does an execution record reference the exact agent version that produced it?
Which correlation identifiers tie messages, tool calls and sub-agent activity into one task?
How are event time and observation or ingestion time recorded separately for agent activity?
What must be captured so that an agent activity can be reconstructed later?

data_elements.name: Run reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an execution record produced by this agent version.

data_elements.name: Conversation identifier
data_elements.description: Correlation identifier for a conversation or thread spanning multiple activities.

data_elements.name: Task identifier
data_elements.description: Correlation identifier for a task and its context across agents.

data_elements.name: Event time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the agent activity occurred.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the record was observed or ingested by the store.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding produces no artefact of its own. It defines reference and correlation semantics carried as inline fields on records owned elsewhere: the execution record is the artefact of WM-AI-004 and the telemetry span is the artefact of the observability finding. Materialising a further artefact here would create a second, divergent copy of run data; only the linkage rules and identifier semantics belong to the agent.

bundles.name: Assurance, observability and risk
bundles.description: What is measured before and during service, what is recorded so behaviour can be audited, and what evidence supports risk and conformity claims.
bundles.rationale: Risk-management guidance requires measurement and management functions; regulation requires activity logging for traceability; telemetry conventions supply a shared attribute vocabulary for agent and tool operations; and published risk taxonomies supply the threat classes an agent deployment must be assessed against.

layers.name: Evaluation and monitoring
layers.description: How the agent is tested before release and watched while in service.

findings.name: Pre-deployment evaluation
findings.description: Capability, safety and robustness evaluations run against a version, acceptance thresholds and who set them, representativeness of the evaluation set, and evaluation provenance.

questions.text: Which capability, safety and robustness evaluations were run against this agent version?
Which acceptance thresholds must be met for release, and who set them?
How well does the evaluation set represent the intended operating context?
When was each evaluation run, on which version, and by whom?

data_elements.name: Evaluation run
data_elements.description: One executed evaluation with suite, scope and configuration.

data_elements.name: Metric result
data_elements.description: Measured value produced by an evaluation.

data_elements.name: Acceptance threshold
data_elements.description: Value a metric must meet or exceed for release.

data_elements.name: Evaluated version
data_elements.description: Agent version the evaluation was run against.

data_elements.name: Evaluated at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the evaluation was executed.

artifacts.name: Agent evaluation report
artifacts.description: Report of evaluation suites, metric results, thresholds, representativeness assessment and run provenance for one agent version.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent version identifier plus sequential evaluation run number; result sets referenced by their own run identifiers.

findings.name: In-service performance monitoring
findings.description: Live indicators showing the agent remains inside its accepted envelope, drift detection, the share of activity sampled for human review, and the response when a threshold is crossed.

questions.text: Which live indicators show that the agent is still performing within its accepted envelope?
How is behavioural drift caused by model, tool or data change detected?
What proportion of agent activity is sampled for human quality review, and how is the sample selected?
What is the defined response when a monitored indicator crosses its alert threshold?

data_elements.name: Monitored metric
data_elements.description: Indicator tracked while the agent is in service.

data_elements.name: Alert threshold
data_elements.description: Value at which a monitored metric raises an alert.

data_elements.name: Review sample rate
data_elements.description: Proportion of activity selected for human review.

data_elements.name: Drift signal
data_elements.description: Coded indicator of behavioural drift.

artifacts.name: Agent monitoring baseline
artifacts.description: Baseline definition of monitored metrics, thresholds, drift signals, sampling strategy and response playbook references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier plus version identifier; superseded baselines retained with their validity windows.

layers.name: Observability and audit
layers.description: What the agent emits so its behaviour can be traced, and how incidents and exceptions are handled and fed back.

findings.name: Telemetry and audit record conformance
findings.description: The attribute schema emitted for agent invocations and tool executions, events that must be logged, controls on recording message content, and log protection and retention.

questions.text: Which telemetry attribute schema is emitted for agent invocations and tool executions?
Which events must be logged so that agent activity remains traceable for its whole lifetime?
Which message content may be recorded in telemetry, and how is sensitive content redacted?
How are logs protected from tampering, and for how long are they kept?

data_elements.name: Telemetry attribute set
data_elements.description: Attribute keys emitted for agent and tool operations.

data_elements.name: Required log event
data_elements.description: Event type that must be logged for traceability.

data_elements.name: Redaction rule
data_elements.description: Rule governing removal or masking of sensitive content in logs.

data_elements.name: Log retention period
data_elements.description: Duration for which agent logs are retained.

data_elements.name: Log integrity method
data_elements.description: Mechanism making log records tamper-evident.

artifacts.name: Agent telemetry profile
artifacts.description: Profile declaring emitted attributes, required events, content recording mode, redaction rules, integrity mechanism and log retention.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier plus version identifier; attribute keys referenced by their governed external names.

findings.name: Incident and exception management
findings.description: What counts as an incident, near miss or serious malfunction, reporting recipients and deadlines, pre-authorised containment actions, and feedback into policy and classification.

questions.text: What counts as an agent incident, near miss or serious malfunction?
To whom and within what deadline must an incident be reported?
Which containment actions are pre-authorised without further approval?
How does an incident feed back into agent policy, limits or classification?

data_elements.name: Incident record
data_elements.description: Structured account of an agent incident or near miss.

data_elements.name: Incident severity
data_elements.description: Coded severity assigned to an incident.

data_elements.name: Reporting deadline
data_elements.description: Maximum time from detection to required report.

data_elements.name: Containment action
data_elements.description: Pre-authorised action to limit incident impact.

data_elements.name: Corrective change reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the policy, limit or classification change made after an incident.

artifacts.name: Agent incident record
artifacts.description: Record of one incident with classification, severity, timeline, containment actions, reports issued and corrective changes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Incident identifier issued by the incident management system; referenced from the agent record rather than duplicated.

layers.name: Risk and conformity evidence
layers.description: The threats the deployment has been assessed against and the documentation that supports risk acceptance and any framework alignment claim.

findings.name: Threat model and conformity evidence
findings.description: Agent-specific threats assessed, residual risks accepted and by whom, the documentation demonstrating alignment to an applicable framework, and the currency of the assessment.

questions.text: Which agent-specific threats has this deployment been assessed against?
Which residual risks are accepted, by whom, and with what compensating controls?
Which documentation set demonstrates alignment to the applicable framework or regulation?
When was the risk assessment last refreshed, and what triggers a re-assessment?

data_elements.name: Threat entry
data_elements.description: One assessed threat with its taxonomy reference.

data_elements.name: Residual risk acceptance
data_elements.description: Recorded acceptance of a residual risk with accepting party and rationale.

data_elements.name: Control mapping
data_elements.description: Mapping from a framework clause to the implementing control and its evidence.

data_elements.name: Assessment date
data_elements.description: Calendar date on which the risk assessment was completed.

data_elements.name: Re-assessment trigger
data_elements.description: Condition that forces the risk assessment to be redone.

artifacts.name: Agent risk and conformity dossier
artifacts.description: Dossier holding the threat model, residual risk acceptances, control-to-clause mapping and supporting evidence for alignment claims.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agent identifier plus sequential assessment number; supersedes prior dossiers without deleting them.

functions.name: Register agent definition
functions.description: Create the authoritative agent record, assign its identifier per the identity priority and bind it to an accountable owner and a regulatory role determination.
preconditions: An accountable organisation is named
A regulatory role and risk determination exists for each jurisdiction
No existing record already claims the same authoritative identifier
effects: The agent becomes citable by other models and records
An append-only lifecycle history is opened with an RFC 3339 entry instant

functions.name: Publish capability descriptor
functions.description: Emit the externally retrievable descriptor listing identity, declared skills, modalities, protocol revisions, endpoints and security schemes, signed so consumers can verify origin.
preconditions: The agent version is in a state permitting external exposure
Each declared skill has supporting evaluation evidence or is marked unevidenced
effects: External consumers can discover and verify the agent's capability surface
Any later change to declared capability invalidates the published digest

functions.name: Grant delegated authority
functions.description: Record a delegation from a principal to the agent with an explicit scope, resource audience, non-delegable exclusions and validity window.
inputs: Requested scope set and resource audiences
preconditions: The granting principal holds the authority being delegated
The requested scope is the minimum required for a declared skill
Target resource audiences are canonical and resolvable
effects: The agent may act on behalf of the principal within the recorded scope until expiry or revocation
The delegation chain depth increases by one for any onward sub-delegation

functions.name: Revoke agent authority
functions.description: Withdraw a delegation or credential immediately and propagate the revocation to sub-agents and dependent grants.
preconditions: The revoking party is the granting principal or an authorised administrator
effects: The agent can no longer present the revoked authority
Downstream sub-delegations derived from the grant are marked invalid

functions.name: Evaluate release readiness
functions.description: Run the required evaluations against a candidate agent version and compare results with the acceptance thresholds set by the responsible authority.
outputs: Pass or fail determination per threshold
preconditions: The candidate version manifest is frozen
Thresholds are recorded with their setting authority
effects: A release gate can be decided on recorded evidence
Coverage gaps are carried forward into the risk dossier

functions.name: Transition lifecycle state
functions.description: Move the agent to a new governed lifecycle state, recording actor, reason, guard evidence and the entry instant.
preconditions: The transition is legal under the recorded state machine
All preconditions for the target state are evidenced
The acting party holds the authority for that transition
effects: The agent's operational permissions change with the state
Prior state entries remain immutable in the append-only history

functions.name: Record oversight intervention
functions.description: Capture a human override, correction, pause or halt with the intervening party, the affected activity and both event and ingestion times.
preconditions: The intervening party is an authorised overseer
The affected activity is identifiable by a correlation identifier
effects: The agent's activity is interrupted or corrected as recorded
Evidence of effective human oversight is preserved for audit

functions.name: Emit agent activity telemetry
functions.description: Emit conformant telemetry for agent invocation and tool execution operations, applying the content recording mode and redaction rules.
preconditions: A telemetry profile is bound to the agent version
Redaction rules are approved by the data steward
effects: Agent activity becomes traceable against a shared attribute vocabulary
Event time and ingestion time are recorded separately on each record

functions.name: Apply retention and erasure
functions.description: Enforce the retention schedule across agent records, logs and memory, honouring legal holds and verifying deletion across replicas and backups.
outputs: Exception list where deletion was blocked
preconditions: No legal hold or open incident references the target items
The retention clock start event is recorded
effects: Expired items are removed from all copies or reported as exceptions
Identity and audit history survive erasure of the underlying content

composition.purpose: An AI system exposes one or more agent actors. System-level obligations, model inventory and market placement remain in WM-AI-001; actor-level authority, tool bindings, memory and oversight remain here so the two are not duplicated.
The agent references the instruction or configuration artefact that governs its behaviour, with a version and pin mode. Instruction text, templating and variables are modelled there, not here.
Each execution record references the exact agent version that produced it, giving execution provenance. Spans, messages, token usage and outcomes belong to WM-AI-004.
The AI agent specialises the generic responsibility-bearing actor. Human principals, approvers and overseers are recorded there and referenced from delegation and accountability findings.

Align agent, activity, entity, attribution, association, delegation and derivation semantics with a published provenance ontology rather than inventing local provenance terms. Alignment only; no conformance is claimed.

composition.target: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions for agent spans
composition.purpose: Align agent and tool operation naming and identifier attributes with a shared telemetry vocabulary. The convention is at Development stability, so the alignment is advisory and versioned separately.

composition.target: A2A Agent Card and task lifecycle
composition.purpose: Align published capability advertisement, skills, modalities, security schemes and card signatures with an inter-agent discovery format. The card name is treated as an alias, never a primary key.

composition.target: Model Context Protocol tool and resource primitives and authorization
composition.purpose: Align tool and resource binding semantics, consent requirements, revision negotiation and audience-bound token handling with a published tool-integration protocol.
Align role determination, risk classification, logging for traceability, human oversight and transparency findings with the applicable regulatory obligations where the agent falls in scope.

composition.target: NIST AI RMF 1.0 and the Generative AI Profile
composition.purpose: Align governance, mapping, measurement and management findings with a voluntary risk framework and its generative-AI companion, noting that neither squarely covers tool-using autonomous agents.

composition.target: NIST SP 800-207 zero trust access policy
composition.purpose: Align per-request authorisation, least privilege and continuous verification of agent actions with zero-trust tenets rather than a bespoke local access theory.

composition.target: Tool or external service model (sibling; no registry identifier assigned in the supplied extract)
composition.purpose: Tool schemas, endpoint contracts and operators belong to a separate subject that this model only references. Marked as an unresolved boundary because the sibling model identifier was not present in the registry extract.

composition.target: Embodied or robotic agent extension (not registered)
composition.purpose: Physical siting, actuation safety and mechanical harm surfaces are outside this model. An extension would be required before applying WM-AI-002 to embodied agents; recorded as a gap rather than asserted as covered.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension MUST name a single accountable owner package for WM-AI-002 records and publish the owning organisation and role before any agent record is created.

The owner package MUST declare which identifier system is authoritative for agent identity in that Dimension and how it maps to protocol-scoped identifiers such as agent-card names and provider-assigned agent identifiers.
The owner package MUST declare jurisdictional scope and the regulatory role held per deployment, since obligations differ between provider and deployer.
The owner package MUST publish retention classes, the policy decision point used for action authorisation, and the escalation route for agent incidents.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint agent identifiers in a stable HTTPS namespace owned by the Dimension, of the form <dimension-base>/world-model/ai/agent/{agent-id}, with version-scoped children of the form .../{agent-id}/version/{version-id}. Never derive a namespace from a mutable display name, an endpoint hostname or a release date. Protocol-scoped names and endpoint URIs are aliases recorded inside the agent's namespace, not primary identifiers, and canonical resource URIs used for token audience binding are kept lowercase, fragment-free and separate from the identity namespace.
registry_links: Vercy world-model registry entry vr.wm-ai-002 and its composition links
Local tool and server allowlist registry referenced by tool bindings
Credential, scope and delegation registry referenced by authority grants
External alignment registries: the OpenTelemetry GenAI attribute registry and the A2A Agent Card schema
Incident management register referenced by incident records

canonicalization_rules: Serialise records as UTF-8 with lexicographically ordered object keys and no insignificant whitespace before hashing or signing; digests are computed over the canonical form, never over a storage projection.
Normalise all time values to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z before comparison, retaining the original offset when local civil time is meaningful.
Resolve every alias to its primary identifier before equality or deduplication tests; alias tables are inputs to canonicalisation, not substitutes for it.
Normalise endpoint and resource URIs to lowercase scheme and host with no fragment and no trailing slash unless the slash is semantically significant.
Represent absent values by omitting the field rather than by empty strings or null placeholders, so that digests are stable across projections.
patch_rules: Patches address content by stable local identifier path, never by array position or display name.
A patch that would change a field frozen at release MUST create a new agent version instead of mutating the existing one.
Every patch carries the acting party, a reason, the event time and the ingestion time, and is retained at least as long as the record it modifies.
Patches to authority scope, tool bindings, memory scope or autonomy level require re-approval by the accountable owner before they take effect.
Lifecycle transitions and log entries are appended, never patched; corrections are new entries that supersede prior ones by explicit reference.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional field or a new code value is backwards compatible; removing a field, narrowing cardinality or changing the meaning of an existing code is breaking and requires a major model version.
Consumers MUST ignore unknown fields and MUST NOT infer semantics from field order or from a storage projection's structure.
Alignments to external standards are versioned independently of this model; upgrading an alignment target never silently changes local semantics and must be recorded as an explicit change.
A protocol revision change in a bound interface is treated as a material change to the agent version, because available primitives differ between revisions.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the agent, such as the deployment platform's agent registry identifier or a provider-assigned hosted agent identifier.
Governed global identifier or IRI minted in the owning Dimension's HTTPS namespace and resolvable to the agent identity record.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when neither of the above exists, recorded together with the reason no governed identifier was available.
Protocol-scoped names, endpoint URIs and display names are aliases only and MUST NOT be used as primary keys; a release date, version date or any other date is never an identifier.
Transient in-memory agent instance identifiers MUST NOT be promoted to primary keys, because they do not survive the process that created them.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with explicit seconds and an explicit UTC offset or the literal Z; a local time without an offset is rejected on ingest. Event time, meaning the instant the agent activity, decision or state transition actually occurred, is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time, meaning the instant the record reached the store, and both are stored whenever they differ. Memory items additionally carry an observation time distinct from their write time. Durations use ISO 8601 duration form and are never substituted for a timestamp; a date-only value is used only where the source is genuinely date-granular and is never treated as an instant.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts are named <agent-id>--<artifact-kind>--<zero-padded-sequence>, with a monotonically increasing sequence per agent and artefact kind, starting at 000001. Sequence numbers are never reused after deletion or supersession, gaps are permitted and meaningful, and no date, timestamp or version-date component appears anywhere in the name.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each artefact stores a digest of its canonical form together with the identifier of the signer or issuing process and the digest algorithm. Artefacts published for external discovery are signed, and consumers MUST verify both digest and signature before trusting any capability, skill or tool description they contain. Tool descriptors, agent cards and retrieved context are treated as untrusted content regardless of digest validity: a valid signature proves origin, not safety.

policies: Least privilege by default: an agent holds no authority that has not been explicitly granted, scoped to a named resource audience and bounded in time.
No token pass-through: a credential presented to the agent MUST NOT be forwarded unchanged to a downstream service; downstream access uses a separately issued, audience-bound credential.

Consent before consequential action: operations with irreversible or externally visible effects require an explicit, recorded human approval unless a standing authorisation covers exactly that action class.
Traceability: every authority change, tool binding change, lifecycle transition and human intervention is recorded with the acting party, event time and ingestion time.
Untrusted descriptor content: tool descriptions, agent cards, memory items and retrieved context are treated as data, never as authority-granting instructions.
No conformance without evidence: alignment to an external standard may be asserted only with a cited clause mapping and dated test or assessment evidence.

read: Any authenticated Dimension member may read agent identity, designation, declared skills, protocol bindings and current lifecycle state.
Reading credential scope maps, delegation grants, memory inventories, incident records or authorisation policies requires an explicit scope grant and is logged.
External consumers read only the published capability descriptor; internal policy, evaluation and risk records are never exposed through the discovery endpoint.
create: Creating an agent record requires an accountable owner, a regulatory role determination per jurisdiction, and an initial lifecycle state entry with an RFC 3339 entry instant.
Creation assigns the identifier per the identity priority and records which system issued it and why lower-priority schemes were not used.
Tool bindings, delegations and credentials may only be created against an existing agent version that is not retired.
update: Non-material updates patch the current version in place with full patch provenance including actor, reason, event time and ingestion time.
Material updates to instructions, tool bindings, authority scope, autonomy level or bound protocol revision create a new agent version and reset release approval.
Lifecycle transitions, consent decisions and interventions are appended as new entries; the previous entry is never edited in place.
delete: Agent records are retired, not deleted; retirement preserves identity, version history and audit records for the applicable retention period.
Hard deletion is permitted only for data subject erasure or unlawful content, is scoped to the affected items, and leaves a tombstone recording what was removed, under which authority and when.
Deletion is blocked while a legal hold, open incident or active investigation references the record, and the block is reported as a retention exception rather than silently ignored.

roles.name: Agent owner (accountable deployer)
responsibilities: Hold named accountability for the agent in production
Approve authority grants, tool bindings and autonomy level
Sign residual risk acceptances and release decisions

roles.name: Agent builder and maintainer
responsibilities: Author and maintain the agent definition and its constituent bindings
Submit versions for release approval with evidence attached
Keep capability descriptors and documentation current with the released version

roles.name: Oversight operator
responsibilities: Monitor live agent behaviour against the accepted envelope
Exercise intervention, pause and stop authority
Record interventions with reason, affected activity and timing

roles.name: Risk and compliance reviewer
responsibilities: Validate regulatory role, risk classification and disclosure duties
Review evaluation evidence and the conformity dossier
Trigger re-assessment when a re-assessment condition occurs

roles.name: Identity and access administrator
responsibilities: Issue, scope, rotate and revoke agent credentials and delegations
Enforce audience binding and the prohibition on token pass-through
Review break-glass grants independently of the requester

roles.name: Data steward
responsibilities: Approve data categories, purposes, memory scope and isolation boundaries
Approve redaction rules for telemetry content recording
Own the retention schedule and authorise erasure and legal holds

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Access to any node is granted per request to an authenticated subject holding an explicit grant for that scope; no access is inherited from network location, asset ownership, session age or from holding a grant on a different node.
exceptions: Break-glass read of authority, credential and memory findings during a live incident: time-boxed, dual-approved, and fully logged with automatic expiry.
Regulator, auditor or supervisory-authority read access to classification, oversight, log and conformity findings under a recorded legal basis and a defined scope.
Public read of the published capability descriptor artefact only, carrying no internal identifiers, policy content or evaluation detail.
Data subject access to memory items about that subject, mediated by the data steward and limited to items attributable to the requester.
audit_requirements: Every read of a credential, delegation, memory inventory, authorisation policy or incident node is logged with subject, grant reference, event time and ingestion time.
Every grant, revocation, scope change and break-glass use is logged and reviewed by a party independent of the requester.
Audit logs are tamper-evident and retained at least as long as the records they describe, and their own access is logged.
Discrepancies between granted scope and observed access are reported as exceptions and fed into the incident process.

Specification URL - model scope, boundaries, bundle, layer and finding structure and question surface
Storage type URL - the concrete projection in use and its canonicalisation, patch and integrity rules
Interface URL - access interface, scopes, authentication and the discovery endpoint contract
Processes URL - CRUD, lifecycle, approval, oversight, incident and retention processes
